Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Draft MAP attached (MAP_Catalyst_v0.2.xlsx). Below is a focused summary so procurement and your GTM partners have something easy to review.

Quick summary (working draft):
- Objective: Two-week pilot (production-like traffic slice) to validate latency, stability, and data handling for the triage use case.
- Success definition (pass/fail): see Acceptance Tests section below. If >= 95% pass across core tests and no critical safety/security findings, proceed to SOW + Dedicated pool provisioning.
- Owners: Redwood will own runtime performance tests and instrumentation; Catalyst will own labeled evaluation sets and business acceptance.
- Cutover window: Target pilot start Oct 19 — end Oct 30.

Acceptance Tests (short):
1) Functional correctness (business acceptance) — pass if F1 >= 0.86 on labeled triage set; manual spot-check concordance >= 90%
2) Latency SLO — 95th percentile <= 220ms at expected concurrency (pilot traffic profile)
3) Concurrency/stability — no server crashes, <1% 5xx errors over 24h
4) Data handling / PII controls — inbound PII redaction verified on sample ingestion; audit logs show request/response retention per agreed policy
5) Safety / hallucination spot checks — domain expert sample review, no confident harmful outputs for PHI scenarios

I've sketched owners in the attachment; open to reassigning. Procurement checklist attached as security_evidence_checklist.pdf.

Thanks Olga — adding the technical acceptance thresholds and owners for running the tests on Redwood side. I'm copying Marcus (runtime lead) and Marissa (CS/close).

Technical acceptance (Redwood responsibilities):
- Throughput: baseline 200 requests/min sustained for 1 hour with 5% token error rate tolerance
- Latency: p95 <= 220ms; measured from edge to end-of-stream with streaming enabled (if using streaming)
- Instrumentation: trace IDs present on every request; logs pushed to our temporary shared S3 for the pilot window
- KV/prefix cache hit test: preloaded prefix cache should reduce token generation CPU by >=20% on warm runs

Owners:
- Marcus Lin — run and report runtime load tests; provide perf dashboard link and csv export by Oct 22
- Ben Carter — coordinate smoke test runbook and rollback criteria
- Olga Petrov — Catalyst business acceptance liaison
- Marissa Cole — coordinate final commercial SOW and DocuSign readiness

Notes on pass/fail: Any single "critical" finding (data exfiltration risk, persistent >5xx errors) will trigger a stop-and-remediate and move the pilot out of the committed cutover.

On the evidence side, Sarah — the security checklist Olga attached covers the SOC2 artifact bundle we can ship; if procurement requires a dedicated SOC2 letter or penetration test report, let us know and we can fast-track.

Thanks — this is very helpful. A couple quick clarifications from procurement:
- We need an estimated SOW value range and a DocuSign-ready statement of work by Oct 16 to hit the Oct 19 start date (even a provisional SOW is fine).
- For security: procurement requires either a current SOC2 Type II report or a letter from your security team confirming controls + an expected date for provisioning KMS/HSM keys for production. We can accept a checklist for the pilot but need the Type II for a full deployment.

For acceptance tests: the business team wants an explicit handoff script for how we'll mark a test "pass" in HubSpot (owner, evidence link, timestamp). Could you add a short column in the MAP spreadsheet that captures: test_owner, evidence_link, pass/fail method?

If Redwood can send the provisional SOW + quick SOC2 note by EOD Friday (Oct 16), procurement will prioritize the DocuSign turnaround. I'll loop legal after we have the SOW.
